```{.quiz-yaml}
id: 18_regression_prediction_error
title: >
  [Placeholder title: why can't the line be perfect?]
questions:
  - id: same_prediction
    type: numeric
    prompt: >
      [Placeholder: two students drank a cup and a half. What does the line
      predict for each of them?]
    answer: 65
    tolerance: 0
    explanation: >
      [Placeholder: 65 for both. A line gives one prediction for each value of
      X, so it can't pass through two different scores at the same X. Unlike
      the temperature line, it has to miss somebody.]

  - id: first_miss
    type: numeric
    prompt: >
      [Placeholder: one of them scored 50. By how many points was the
      prediction too high?]
    answer: 15
    tolerance: 0
    explanation: >
      [Placeholder: 65 − 50 = 15. That miss is the prediction error.]

  - id: shift_down
    type: numeric
    prompt: >
      [Placeholder: move the whole line down five points. How far off is the
      prediction now for the student who scored 65?]
    answer: 5
    tolerance: 0
    explanation: >
      [Placeholder: we'd now predict 60, so 5 points off there, though closer
      for the student who scored 50. Fixing one miss makes another worse.]

  - id: best_single_guess
    type: numeric
    prompt: >
      [Placeholder: if we could give these two students only one prediction,
      which number would make the sum of their squared misses smallest?]
    answer: 57.5
    tolerance: 0.01
    hint: >
      [Placeholder: Chapter 4. Which single value minimizes the sum of squared
      deviations?]
    explanation: >
      [Placeholder: their mean, 57.5. Squared misses of 7.5 and 7.5 give 112.5,
      less than 225 + 0 for a guess of 65. The best line does the same thing
      for all seven students at once: it makes the total squared error as
      small as possible.]
```
